audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Timothy, Spirit travel direction, Macedonian vision, Lydia, enslaved divination girl, Philippi imprisonment, earthquake, jailer household, citizen-rights release.

verses.restored: He came also to Derbe and to Lystra. Look, a certain disciple was there named Timothy, son of a trusting Judean woman and a Greek father.

familiar.text: Then came he to Derbe and Lystra: and, behold, a certain disciple was there, named Timotheus, the son of a certain woman, which was a Jewess, and believed; but his father was a Greek:

verses.restored: He was well witnessed by the siblings in Lystra and Iconium.

familiar.text: Which was well reported of by the brethren that were at Lystra and Iconium.

verses.restored: Paul wanted this one to go out with him; taking him, he circumcised him because of the Judeans in those places, for they all knew his father was Greek.

familiar.text: Him would Paul have to go forth with him; and took and circumcised him because of the Jews which were in those quarters: for they knew all that his father was a Greek.

verses.restored: As they were passing through the cities, they were delivering to them to guard the decrees judged by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And as they went through the cities, they delivered them the decrees for to keep, that were ordained of the apostles and elders which were at Jerusalem.

verses.restored: Therefore the assemblies were being strengthened in the trust and were increasing in number day by day.

familiar.text: And so were the churches established in the faith, and increased in number daily.

verses.restored: They went through the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been forbidden by the holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia.

familiar.text: Now when they had gone throughout Phrygia and the region of Galatia, and were forbidden of the Holy Ghost to preach the word in Asia,

verses.restored: Coming near Mysia, they were attempting to go into Bithynia, and the Spirit of Jesus did not permit them.

familiar.text: After they were come to Mysia, they assayed to go into Bithynia: but the Spirit suffered them not.

verses.restored: Passing by Mysia, they came down to Troas.

familiar.text: And they passing by Mysia came down to Troas.

verses.restored: A vision appeared to Paul during the night: a certain Macedonian man was standing and urging him, saying, Come over into Macedonia and help us.

familiar.text: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.

verses.restored: When he saw the vision, immediately we sought to go out into Macedonia, concluding that the Divine had called us to announce good news to them.

familiar.text: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.

verses.restored: Putting out to sea from Troas, we ran straight to Samothrace, and the next day to Neapolis,

familiar.text: Therefore loosing from Troas, we came with a straight course to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis;

verses.restored: and from there to Philippi, which is a leading city of that district of Macedonia, a Roman colony. We were remaining in this city some days.

familiar.text: And from thence to Philippi, which is the chief city of that part of Macedonia, and a colony: and we were in that city abiding certain days.

verses.restored: On the Sabbath day, we went outside the gate by a river where we supposed there was a place of prayer, and sitting down, we were speaking to the women who had gathered.

familiar.text: And on the sabbath we went out of the city by a river side, where prayer was wont to be made; and we sat down, and spake unto the women which resorted thither.

verses.restored: A certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, revering the Divine, was hearing. The Lord opened her heart to pay attention to the things spoken by Paul.

familiar.text: And a certain woman named Lydia, a seller of purple, of the city of Thyatira, which worshipped God, heard us: whose heart the Lord opened, that she attended unto the things which were spoken of Paul.

verses.restored: When she and her household were baptized, she urged us, saying, If you have judged me faithful to the Lord, come into my house and remain. And she prevailed upon us.

familiar.text: And when she was baptized, and her household, she besought us, saying, If ye have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, come into my house, and abide there. And she constrained us.

verses.restored: It happened as we were going to prayer, a certain enslaved girl having a spirit of python/divination met us, who provided much profit to her masters by fortune-telling.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as we went to prayer, a certain damsel possessed with a spirit of divination met us, which brought her masters much gain by soothsaying:

verses.restored: This one, following Paul and us, cried out, saying, These humans are servants of the Most High Divine, who announce to you a way of salvation/healing.

familiar.text: The same followed Paul and us, and cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God, which shew unto us the way of salvation.

verses.restored: She was doing this for many days. Paul, being greatly troubled, turned and said to the spirit, I command you in the name of Jesus Messiah to come out from her. And it came out that very hour.

familiar.text: And this did she many days. But Paul, being grieved, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee in the name of Jesus Christ to come out of her. And he came out the same hour.

verses.restored: Her masters, seeing that the hope of their profit had gone out, seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers.

familiar.text: And when her masters saw that the hope of their gains was gone, they caught Paul and Silas, and drew them into the marketplace unto the rulers,

verses.restored: Bringing them to the magistrates, they said, These humans, being Judeans, are disturbing our city,

familiar.text: And brought them to the magistrates, saying, These men, being Jews, do exceedingly trouble our city,

verses.restored: and are proclaiming customs that are not lawful for us to receive or practice, being Romans.

familiar.text: And teach customs, which are not lawful for us to receive, neither to observe, being Romans.

verses.restored: The crowd rose together against them, and the magistrates, tearing off their garments, commanded them to be beaten with rods.

familiar.text: And the multitude rose up together against them: and the magistrates rent off their clothes, and commanded to beat them.

verses.restored: Having laid many blows on them, they threw them into prison, commanding the jailer to guard them securely.

familiar.text: And when they had laid many stripes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely:

verses.restored: Having received such a command, he threw them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.

familiar.text: Who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and made their feet fast in the stocks.

verses.restored: About midnight, Paul and Silas, praying, were singing hymns to the Divine, and the prisoners were listening to them.

familiar.text: And at midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.

verses.restored: Suddenly a great earthquake happened, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken. Immediately all the doors were opened, and everyone's bonds were loosened.

familiar.text: And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken: and immediately all the doors were opened, and every one’s bands were loosed.

verses.restored: The jailer, becoming awake and seeing the prison doors opened, drew the sword and was about to kill himself, supposing the prisoners had escaped.

familiar.text: And the keeper of the prison awaking out of his sleep, and seeing the prison doors open, he drew out his sword, and would have killed himself, supposing that the prisoners had been fled.

verses.restored: But Paul cried with a great voice, saying, Do nothing harmful to yourself, for we are all here.

familiar.text: But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm: for we are all here.

verses.restored: Calling for lights, he rushed in, and trembling, fell before Paul and Silas.

familiar.text: Then he called for a light, and sprang in, and came trembling, and fell down before Paul and Silas,

verses.restored: Bringing them outside, he said, Lords, what must I do to be saved/healed?

familiar.text: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?

verses.restored: They said, Trust upon the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved/healed, you and your house.

familiar.text: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.

verses.restored: They spoke the word of the Lord to him, together with all those in his house.

familiar.text: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.

verses.restored: Taking them in that hour of the night, he washed their wounds, and he was baptized at once, he and all his household.

familiar.text: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.

verses.restored: Bringing them up into the house, he set a table before them, and rejoiced with his whole household, having trusted the Divine.

familiar.text: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.

verses.restored: When day came, the magistrates sent the officers, saying, Release those humans.

familiar.text: And when it was day, the magistrates sent the serjeants, saying, Let those men go.

verses.restored: The jailer reported these words to Paul: The magistrates have sent to release you. Now therefore go out and travel in peace.

familiar.text: And the keeper of the prison told this saying to Paul, The magistrates have sent to let you go: now therefore depart, and go in peace.

verses.restored: But Paul said to them, Having beaten us publicly without trial, men who are Romans, they threw us into prison; and now do they cast us out secretly? No indeed. Let them come themselves and bring us out.

familiar.text: But Paul said unto them, They have beaten us openly uncondemned, being Romans, and have cast us into prison; and now do they thrust us out privily? nay verily; but let them come themselves and fetch us out.

verses.restored: The officers reported these words to the magistrates, and they were afraid when they heard that they were Romans.

familiar.text: And the serjeants told these words unto the magistrates: and they feared, when they heard that they were Romans.

verses.restored: Coming, they appealed to them, and bringing them out, asked them to leave the city.

familiar.text: And they came and besought them, and brought them out, and desired them to depart out of the city.

verses.restored: Going out from the prison, they entered Lydia's house; and seeing the siblings, they encouraged them and departed.

familiar.text: And they went out of the prison, and entered into the house of Lydia: and when they had seen the brethren, they comforted them, and departed.
